paper: Yuan & Chen 2023 - Hexagonal close-packed skyrmion lattice in ultrathin ferroelectric PbTiO3 films

open_questions.question: Does a hexagonal close-packed polar SkX emerge SPONTANEOUSLY from a labyrinth/stripe domain state under increasing Ez, without seeding pre-formed skyrmions?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The paper's central claim is field-INDUCED emergence (L -> Sk&L -> SkX). Our reduced 2D LGD reproduced SkX stability and its field-driven destruction, but the SkX had to be seeded; spontaneous nucleation is the harder, unproven half of the headline.
open_questions.next_step: Add the full 3D depolarization field (open-circuit boundary with screening theta) and a Landau expansion with the paper's Haun PbTiO3 coefficients [Ref 56], then quench from a random state at fixed Ez to test whether SkX nucleates without seeds.

open_questions.question: Is the simulated SkX genuinely Neel-type with center-convergent/divergent top/bottom planes and a purely out-of-plane middle plane, as the paper reports?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The paper distinguishes its Neel-type SkX from the Bloch-walled skyrmion bubbles of PTO/STO superlattices [Ref 33]; the wall type is a physical fingerprint of the strain/electrostatic balance.
open_questions.next_step: Extend to a 3D slab (Nz ~ 6 cells) and inspect the through-thickness rotation of P at a single core; verify Ising-type (out-of-plane) connecting wall vs Bloch-type.

open_questions.question: Does the hexagonal lattice constant w obey Kittel scaling, w^2 proportional to film thickness h, over 5 nm < h < 13 nm?
open_questions.why_it_matters: This quantitative scaling law (w=13.6 nm at h=6 nm, w=20.5 nm at h=11.2 nm) is a second, independent testable prediction distinct from the field-collapse headline.
open_questions.next_step: Run 3D simulations at h = 6, 8, 11 nm, extract nearest-core distance from the SkX autocorrelation, and regress w^2 vs h.

open_questions.question: Where exactly do the S->SkX and L->SkX transition boundaries sit in the T-E phase diagram, and is the low-T-L / high-T-S inverse transition reproduced?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The paper reports SkX only between 300-500 K and an unusual inverse L->S transition on heating; the phase-boundary topology is a strong test of the free-energy balance.
open_questions.next_step: Add a temperature-dependent Landau coefficient a(T)=a0(T-T0) and a thermal-noise TDGL sweep to map n_sky and |Q| over a (T, Ez) grid.

open_questions.question: How sensitive is the SkX stability window to the screening factor theta and misfit strain, which the paper fixes at theta=0.6 and eps=-1.0%?
open_questions.why_it_matters: These two boundary-condition parameters set the depolarization/anisotropy balance; the whole SkX-existence region may shrink or vanish outside a narrow range, affecting experimental realizability.
open_questions.next_step: Sweep theta in {0.4,0.6,0.8} and eps in {-0.5%,-1.0%,-2.0%} in the depolarization kernel amplitude and anisotropy K_z, and record the Ez-width of the |Q|>0 window.

next_steps: Promote the 2D single-surface model to a 3D slab (Nx x Ny x ~6) with a proper Poisson-solved depolarization field.
Replace reduced coefficients with the Haun et al. PbTiO3 Landau parameters and physical gradient/electrostrictive constants to recover MV/cm-scale field thresholds.
Reproduce the full T-E phase diagram (Fig. 3) and the Kittel w^2 vs h scaling (Fig. 4) as two additional quantitative checkpoints.
Cross-check topological charge with an independent finite-difference Pontryagin integral alongside the Berg-Luscher lattice method.
